pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/mcp/src/prompts.rs:74 The MCP prompt journeys name tools in hand-written prose, and no test or load-time check confirms that each name exists in the generated tools/list roster, so renaming a tool would leave these instructions pointing at a tool the dispatcher rejects.

techniques.evidence: crates/mcp/src/prompts.rs:74 tools/list itself is generated from lighttrack-contract and filtered to the active set (tools.rs:26), but the tool names in the prompt text are hand-kept and have no sync check against that registry. The only test (get_weaves_in_arguments) asserts the same hard-coded string.
crates/mcp/src/prompts.rs:73 Each prompt opens with the ask itself, not a role or expertise claim. Numbered steps follow, and a closing step defines when the task is done.

crates/mcp/src/prompts.rs:148 Missing arguments get a declared default or a fallback branch, which is right. But `by` is declared as the enum customer|product and is never checked, so any string the caller passes is written into the prompt text.
crates/mcp/src/prompts.rs:58 One assembler (`get`) builds the single task-layer message for each prompt family from typed args. No call site appends text afterwards.

crates/mcp/src/resources.rs:151 An oversized resource body replaces recoverable span payloads with a pointer that names the way back and the byte count. The structural view is kept, and a floor (MIN_ELIDABLE) stops elision from making small fields bigger.

crates/mcp/src/resources.rs:125 The elision shipped without any counter of how often a consumer follows the get_event pointer back, so nothing can tell whether the 24 KiB trigger is too aggressive or too timid.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/engine/src/anthropic_api.rs:42 The Anthropic API output ceiling is a constant sized for a judge verdict (per the comment above it), yet every Anthropic-API generation uses it, including candidate generation and the gateway's generate_chat. A max_tokens stop comes back as EngineError::Truncated with no retry at a higher ceiling, and the output_tokens recorded on every success never feed the number.

techniques.evidence: crates/engine/src/anthropic_api.rs:42 The ceiling is a stated preference ('generous headroom'), not derived from a percentile of observed lengths. Truncation is not escalated per call. The 64k high-effort ceiling is correctly scoped to the effort levels that need it, but its basis is a vendor floor, which the technique says is not a derivation.

crates/engine/src/chat.rs:125 One ChatRequest vocabulary gives each adapter its own wire view. The system prompt stays a dedicated leading field (and a `system` body field on Anthropic) instead of being concatenated into the turns.
crates/engine/src/chat.rs:29 Turns carry only text plus OpenAI tool_calls and ids. No provider-sealed reasoning or signature metadata is stored or replayed, so there is nothing to seal per endpoint.

crates/engine/src/anthropic_api.rs:131 Every adapter re-sends the caller's full turn list statelessly. Neither client-side nor provider-side compaction or context editing is used, so there are no competing owners.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/prompt.rs:89 Core stores prompt text as an opaque string on an immutable version row and never renders, budgets, compacts or sends a prompt. A search of crates/core found no compaction, cache breakpoints, max_tokens or template rendering, so assembly happens outside this context.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/gateway/src/wire.rs:111 Every system/developer message, wherever it sits in the conversation, is lifted out of the turn list and joined into the leading system field (line 136). A mid-conversation system message therefore moves to byte zero, which is the meaning-preserving but position-destroying proxy rewrite that the technique says breaks prefix stability.

techniques.evidence: crates/gateway/src/wire.rs:111 The technique's 'last writer is not always yours' section asks to hoist only the leading run of system content and demote later system messages in place. Here every one is hoisted.

crates/gateway/src/wire.rs:28 The caller's chosen max_tokens is thrown away, so HTTP targets fall back to the engine default (4096 on the Anthropic API). A Truncated result is then classed Terminal (failover.rs:76), with neither escalation nor failover.

crates/gateway/src/wire.rs:39 Inbound messages keep only role, text content (non-text parts are refused) and tool_calls/tool_call_id. No sealed provider metadata survives intake to be replayed on another seat after failover.
